s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pruritic skin lesions with hyperkeratotic plaques
salient_findings: Pruritic lesions on the scrotum and buttock
Annular gray hyperkeratotic plaques with atrophic center and elevated edge
Hyperkeratosis, irregular papillomatosis, and parakeratotic columns on histopathology
key_facts: 10-year history of pruritic lesions
Lesions located on scrotum, buttock, groin, and intergluteal cleft
Previous treatment at local clinic with little improvement
No relevant medical history
No family history of similar skin problems
Normal or negative routine blood work, syphilis serologies, and HIV testing
Histopathological examination revealed hyperkeratosis and parakeratotic columns
Perivascular infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis
No inguinal adenopathy

shortlist.label: Darier disease
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic plaques and dyskeratotic keratinocytes match Darier disease

shortlist.label: Porokeratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Annular plaques with atrophic centers and cornoid lamellae are characteristic of porokeratosis

shortlist.label: Grover disease
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic lesions and hyperkeratotic plaques are consistent with Grover disease

shortlist.label: Hailey-Hailey disease
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic plaques and perivascular infiltration of lymphocytes are seen in Hailey-Hailey disease

shortlist.label: Lichen simplex chronicus
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic pruritic lesions with hyperkeratotic plaques are consistent with lichen simplex chronicus

raw.rationale: The presence of hyperkeratosis, irregular papillomatosis, parakeratotic columns (cornoid lamella), and dyskeratotic keratinocytes in the histopathological examination are characteristic features of porokeratosis, which matches the clinical presentation of well-defined, annular gray hyperkeratotic plaques with an atrophic center and a slightly elevated edge.

rejected.label: Darier disease
rejected.why: Darier disease typically presents with greasy, crusted, or wart-like lesions in seborrheic areas, which does not match the clinical description provided.

rejected.label: Grover disease
rejected.why: Grover disease is characterized by sudden onset of pruritic papules, which does not fit the 10-year history of lesions described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Hailey-Hailey disease
rejected.why: Hailey-Hailey disease typically presents with flaccid blisters or erosions in the intertriginous areas, which is not consistent with the well-defined, annular gray hyperkeratotic plaques described.

rejected.label: Lichen simplex chronicus
rejected.why: Lichen simplex chronicus is characterized by thickened, hyperpigmented plaques due to chronic scratching, which does not match the specific histopathological features found in this case.
